Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0003.JPG.tag_notes: Looking up the brick-and-stone façade of The Anglo Portuguese Telephone Co. Ltd building, its name spelled out in relief lettering along the cornice line. Arched fanlight windows, rusticated piers and diamond panels mark this early-20th-century company headquarters in central Lisbon.

subject: Façade
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0007.JPG.tag_notes: The roofless stone gable of the Carmo Convent ruin (Convento do Carmo, Chiado), its empty window opening framing nothing but blue sky, a cross still crowning the peak. True 14th-century Gothic left as a ruin after the 1755 earthquake — tagged Gothic Revival as the closest vocab fit.

subject: Streetscape
Skyline
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0013.JPG.tag_notes: Elevated view over Rossio (Baixa): the Neo-Manueline pinnacles and lace-carved cornice of Rossio Station in the foreground, the lettered pediment of the Teatro Nacional beyond a Portuguese flag, and pastel houses stacking up the hillside. Pedestrians and a car wait at the crossing below.

subject: Skyline
Façade
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0016.JPG.tag_notes: Tighter frame on the same Rossio scene: Rossio Station's twisted Neo-Manueline spires against the 'TEATRO NACIONAL' inscription and flag of the theater beyond, terracotta roofs and a lime-green corner house climbing the Baixa hillside behind.

subject: Skyline
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0017.JPG.tag_notes: The crenellated towers of Castelo de São Jorge flying the Portuguese flag on its pine-topped hill, seen across a sea of terracotta rooftops, dormers and chimney vents from a Baixa rooftop; a red construction crane cuts across the castle wall.

subject: Detail
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0020.JPG.tag_notes: Golden-hour light on the crown of the Arco da Rua Augusta at Praça do Comércio (Baixa): the allegory of Glory holding two wreaths above Valor and Genius, over the Latin inscription VIRTUTIBUS MAIORUM. Tram wires and a streetlamp cross the frame.

subject: Murals
Detail
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0024.JPG.tag_notes: A Baroque blue-and-white azulejo tile panel glowing under night lighting behind an iron railing: a Marian devotional scene with the crowned Virgin and Child among clouds, angels and flanking palm trees. Azulejo tilework is the precise style — not in the vocab, so tagged Other.

subject: Streetscape
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0030.JPG.tag_notes: Dusk in an Alfama alley: a single wall-mounted lantern throws amber light onto a weathered stucco wall while the sky burns violet behind the rooftops. The tiled street plaque reads Escadinhas de Santo Estêvão; wrought-iron balconies and cobbles sit in deep shadow.

subject: Streetscape
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0031.JPG.tag_notes: Blue-hour on an Alfama stair street near Santo Estêvão: an ornate wrought-iron lantern washes the whitewashed house fronts in warm orange against a deep indigo sky, a handrail leading up the worn steps between them.

subject: Façade
Detail
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0033.JPG.tag_notes: The Neo-Manueline clock tower of Sintra's town hall (Câmara Municipal de Sintra) against a deep blue sky — a tiled green-and-white chevron spire crowned by a gilded armillary sphere, corner pinnacles and a crenellated parapet; a stone Cross of the Order of Christ finial rises at lower left. Neo-Manueline is the precise style, tagged Other.

subject: Façade
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0034.JPG.tag_notes: The ochre-yellow wing of Pena Palace in Sintra framed by winter branches: Islamic-style crenellations, horseshoe-arched windows with flower boxes, a zinc dome and a minaret-like turret topped by a yellow onion cupola. 19th-century Romanticist revival — tagged Other.

subject: Façade
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0035.JPG.tag_notes: Pena Palace from the garden terraces below: dark lichen-stained ramparts and a bartizan turret in the foreground, the yellow crenellated tower rising behind, with palms, agaves and red aloe flowers filling the slope. Sintra's Romanticist hilltop palace, tagged Other.

subject: Façade
People
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0037.JPG.tag_notes: Pena Palace's entrance front in Sintra: the lavender tile-clad wing with rose windows and arched balconies, twin turrets capped in yellow-tiled domes, and the Moorish-crenellated yellow gatehouse with the Portuguese flag; visitors line the rampart walk.

subject: Detail
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0038.JPG.tag_notes: Abstract sliver of Pena Palace, Sintra: through the shadowed curve of a whitewashed arch, a wedge of blue sky and the yellow tower with its white arched mullioned window, sunlight raking the stucco. Light-and-shadow study of the Romanticist palace.

subject: Façade
People
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0039.JPG.tag_notes: Inside Pena Palace's terrace court, Sintra: the ox-blood red clock tower with corner turrets and its white clock face rises over yellow crenellated walls and white lace parapets; tourists cluster on the studded bartizan terrace in the foreground.

subject: Landscape
Skyline
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0041.JPG.tag_notes: Hazy long view from the Sintra hills toward Lisbon: umbrella pines and cedars in silhouette, and on the misty horizon the towers of the Ponte 25 de Abril suspension bridge over the Tagus river and the Cristo Rei statue at Almada — bridge, water and statue dissolving into the grey.

subject: Detail
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0045.JPG.tag_notes: Pena Palace window detail, Sintra: an open white casement in a stone arch on the saffron-yellow stucco wall, throwing hard diagonal shadows, beneath a carved Gothic quatrefoil parapet frieze studded with ball ornaments and a strip of patterned tile.

subject: Detail
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0046.JPG.tag_notes: Peering from deep shadow into Pena Palace's inner courtyard, Sintra: a sunlit wall of geometric Hispano-Moresque azulejo tiles above a stone arcade with slender columns, the shadow of a spire cast diagonally across the pattern.

subject: Detail
Façade
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0048.JPG.tag_notes: Pena Palace courtyard elevation, Sintra: bands of geometric azulejo tile in green, rust and white wrap a loggia of marble columns and stone arches, with an iron railing above and a carved Manueline pinnacle sprouting grotesque faces at right. Strong raking shadow splits the frame.

subject: Detail
Façade
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0049.JPG.tag_notes: Looking up at Pena Palace's red clock tower, Sintra: weathered ox-blood render, stone corner turrets with conical caps, the white clock face, and in the foreground a lion gargoyle, carved mask and a pinnacle topped with a cross above a band of patterned azulejos.

subject: Interior
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0050.JPG.tag_notes: A state bedroom inside Pena Palace, Sintra, in dim amber light: a canopy bed with draped cream-and-gold curtains beneath a Gothic ribbed vault, a glazed della-Robbia-style Madonna and Child relief on the wall, a gilt-framed portrait and a small figurine on the Empire-style headboard.

subject: People
Detail
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0052.JPG.tag_notes: FLAG(remove): Posed portrait of a travel companion, not documentary photography: a young woman stands centered in the archway, body squared to the lens and smiling directly at the camera, filling the frame while the Pena cloister behind her is reduced to backdrop. The first-pass note ('a visitor smiles in silhouette') reads it as an anonymous visitor, but the framing is a snapshot of someone the photographer knows. — A visitor smiles in silhouette under a stone arch of Pena Palace's Manueline cloister, Sintra: behind her, the two-tier arcaded patio with green geometric azulejo walls, a blue-and-white mosaic floor, potted ferns and palms.

subject: Landscape
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0055.JPG.tag_notes: Through a palace casement window at Pena, Sintra: the crenellated ramparts of the Castelo dos Mouros (Moorish Castle) riding their boulder-strewn ridge, with the town below and the hazy Sintra plain stretching to the horizon. Medieval Moorish fortification, tagged Other.

subject: Façade
Portugal Dec '25/Lisbon 1/IMG_0058.JPG.tag_notes: Pena Palace against a streaked blue sky, Sintra: the great yellow drum tower under its grey zinc dome with icicle-like carved drip ornament at the parapet, beside the lavender tile-clad wing with Manueline arched windows and red flower boxes; chimney pots line the roofline below.
